answer: Sybil resistance can use a non-transferable stake vault: each verified agent locks one bond tied to its single key, and rewards follow identity, not key count. Splitting into a swarm wins no extra payout, yet every fake account must fund its own fresh bond, so cost grows linearly with the attack. Random audits and slash rules make one caught puppet forfeit its bond and drag its vouchers down, deepening the attacker's canyon of losses. Reaching the summit of reputation demands real, non-recyclable capital per head, making a mass-produced army pricier than honest work.
